messages:
carla.morris: Quick follow-up from the egress patterns RFC — we need to pick a path for customer-isolated egress. TL;DR: two viable proposals (A: per-customer NAT pools + per-tenant IGW, B: shared regional egress with tagged SNAT). Need ops, cost, and rollout tradeoffs.
ben_li: Can you bullet the main tradeoffs again? my brain fogged after the meeting :sweat_smile:
carla.morris: Sure — succinctly: A) Strong isolation (dedicated IPs per customer) -> easier customer audit, simpler IP allowlisting for customers, but higher IP and NAT gateway cost + more routing rules. B) Shared pool -> lower cost, simpler infra, but increases complexity for tracking customer source IPs and harder for customers that require single static IP.
dinesh: Also add failure modes: A has more objects to manage but degradation is isolated per-customer. B has single region blast radius for egress failure unless we add overflow plumbing.
maya_ops: From an ops perspective, A means we need an automated IP lifecycle: allocate on onboarding, rotation, deprovision on offboarding, and a reconciliation job. Can we automate that with existing operator?
sam.g: We can — infra-bot can emit a ticket when allocation disagrees, but the real cost is elastic IP limits per-account in cloud. For large customers we may hit soft limits quickly.
ben_li: What about hybrid: default shared pool (B) + opt-in dedicated IPs for customers who request/ pay for them? That seems pragmatic.
carla.morris: Hybrid is appealing. The RFC discussed opt-in but didn't formalize routing semantics. Questions: 1) how do we route requests from a tenant pinned to dedicated IP to the dedicated NAT vs shared? 2) How does fallback work if dedicated NAT capacity is exhausted?
dinesh: Implementation sketch: tag tenant routes in VPC with route table entries that point to a dedicated egress ENI/NAT instance. Default route uses the regional egress ALB/NAT. Fallback semantics: if dedicated NAT is unresponsive, we failover to shared but mark the tenant as degraded and notify customer + set a short-lived reverse-proxy header identifying failover.
maya_ops: We need fail-open vs fail-closed policy decision. Some customers require fail-closed (no traffic if dedicated path fails). Others prefer fail-open. We should make this per-customer flag in the billing/onboard API.
ben_li: Agree. Also need to think about metrics: per-tenant egress bytes, error rates, and latency variance. If we put opt-in behind a paid feature, we must ensure billing aligns with measured egress usage.
infra-bot: [automation] Created infra issue #ENG-4321: allocate EIP pool lifecycle controller and reconciliation job.
sam.g: Another operational concern: DNS and TLS flows. For services that do client TLS with SNI, source IP doesn't matter, but for allowlisting we rely on these IPs. We'll need docs and a sample iptables snippet for customers to test.
carla.morris: Good point. We should publish an 'egress onboarding runbook' with steps: 1) request IP 2) validate with tcpdump or curl from our egress box 3) provide allowlist snippet.
dinesh: For rollout plan: phase 1 = hybrid opt-in behind feature flag (no dedicated allocation automation; manual provisioning for early adopters). phase 2 = automation + reconciliation + per-tenant routing. phase 3 = scale optimizations (shared pool autoscaling, NAT warm pool).
maya_ops: Phase 1 ops checklist: manual EIP assignment, route table add, smoke test, inform customer, observe 48h. Need playbook for emergency rollback (route remove + annotate).
ben_li: Risk register: - IP limit exhaustion - Route table churn/management scale - Cross-AZ hairpin latency in some clouds - Accounting mismatch (customer thinks dedicated IP but we silently failover)
carla.morris: On the accounting point: require customer-visible status endpoint with 'egress_state' (DEDICATED | SHARED | FAILOVER) surfaced in the Console and via webhook. That avoids surprises.
sam.g: Implementation detail: add a header x-rw-egress-state on outbound egress logs for internal debugging and include hashed tenant id to map to billing events. Example: x-rw-egress: tenant=tid-12345;state=DEDICATED
dinesh: Regarding routing primitives — prefer route table approach over sidecar NAT because route table change is simple and cloud-native. Sidecar requires per-pod/container changes and is heavy.
maya_ops: Route table changes will require IAM guardrails. We must restrict who can write route entries and make the operator the sole actor.
ben_li: Can we simulate capacity limits before rollout? e.g., a chaos test that tears down a dedicated NAT and verifies failover signals and onboarding webhooks?
carla.morris: Yes — create a staged chaos plan: test in staging with a single tenant, then alpha with a low-risk customer, then gradual ramp. We'll include metrics SLOs for failover detection (<30s) and notification (<5m).
sam.g: For on-costs: we should estimate EIP per-customer cost. Proposal: include a surcharge option in billing UI + discounted bundled IPs for enterprise contracts.
maya_ops: For deprovision flow, we need a retention policy: hold IPs for N days after offboard (N configurable, default 7) to reduce immediate reuse fallout.
ben_li: Anything about cross-region customers? Some customers span regions and want sticky egress IP per-region. We'll allow per-region dedicated allocation and document that it requires separate onboarding per-region.
carla.morris: Action items: - @dinesh: draft operator changes (route table tags + failover signals) - @sam.g: spec a header and logging changes + metrics mapping - @maya_ops: ops runbook for manual provisioning + rollback - @ben_li: billing proposal for dedicated IPs and opt-in UX
carla.morris: Let's reconvene in 48h with PRs/notes. If anyone wants to add blockers now, drop them below. :thumbsup:
ben_li: :thumbsup:
dinesh: I'll add a short Terraform sketch to the issue for the operator to consume.
maya_ops: Added an early checklist to #ENG-4321.
infra-bot: [automation] Updated ENG-4321 status -> in_progress (assigned: dinesh, sam.g, maya_ops).
carla.morris: Thanks all — I'll put the hybrid plan in the RFC follow-up doc and link to ENG-4321.
